### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
Hydro converts conserved state to primitives, constructs directional fluxes, limits species transport, takes the
geometric divergence, adds forcing and gravity work, and applies the optional vertical implicit correction.
Physics choices are owned by their chapters and @sec-ch12-matrix.
Order: code map; no independent measured convergence order.
No defining equation: this section maps control flow or data ownership.
:::

Hydro converts conserved state to primitives, constructs directional fluxes, limits species transport, takes the
geometric divergence, adds forcing and gravity work, and applies the optional vertical implicit correction. Its result
is an increment, not an updated conserved state.

### Derivation

No separate derivation: this section describes an interface or control-flow path. Numerical operators are derived in
their owning chapters.

### Numerical method

The seven sections are primitive conversion; x1 reconstruction, Riemann flux, sedimentation and process-seam
averaging; horizontal left/right states and panel exchange; horizontal fluxes and positivity; divergence with
geometric sources; forcing and gravity work; and implicit correction. Communication occurs inside this pipeline as
well as in the driver wrapper: x1 process-seam fluxes, panel states and donor factors must be synchronized at their
own use sites. Disabled directions and unresolved dimensions are gated separately. Orders and wall closures are
derived by the owning physics chapters.

@fig-ch01-hydro-flow shows the data or call sequence.

### Limits

The implicit time step is stage-weighted only for an integrator with three stages. A direct hydro caller that has not
published a valid stage receives a one-time warning and uses the full time step. Same-process x1 seam flux averaging
is explicitly excluded by the cited code. Neither case is newly measured here.
